messages.subject: Multigroup SEM - Latent mean differences
parts:
Hi everybody,

Im doing multigroup SEM and compare the latent means 9 different groups (study subjects like social science, natural science).

sem.model <- Success =~ Item 1 + Item 2 + Item 3
Motivation_v1 =~ Item 4 + Item 5
Motivation_v2 =~ Item 6 + Item 7
Success ~ Motivation_v1 + Moitvation_v2

To compare the latent means, loadings and manifest intercepts were restricted to be the same across the groups (study subjects)

Model <- sem(sem.model  data = data1, group = "subjects", group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))

lavaan now automatically sets the latent intercepts of the group with the most participants (in my case social science) to 0, so that the latent intercepts of the other groups can be interpreted as the difference to this group (e.g. students of social science have a higher motivational variable 1 than students of natural science)

In a next step i want to use a different subject as my reference group (i.e. set the latent intercept to 0), so that i can compare this specific subject to the others. My question is: How can i manually choose which group i use as a reference group and set to 0 (instead of relying on the automatic process of lavaan)?

Thank you for your help!
Jonas

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup SEM - Latent mean differences
parts:
> lavaan now automatically sets the latent intercepts of the group with
> the most participants (in my case social science) to 0

That is simply because that group appeared as the first group in the
dataset. You can change the 'order' of the groups by using the
group.label= argument.

Yves.
